q: 1. A bending moment may be defined as
options: arithmetic sum of the moments of all the forces on either side of the section
arithmetic sum of the forces on either sides of the section
algebraic sum of the moments of all the forces on either side of the section
explain: Bending moment at a section is defined as the algebraic (signed) sum of moments of all forces acting on either side of that section, since signs (sagging/hogging) matter.

q: 2. At either end of a plane frame, maximum number of possible transverse shear forces, are
explain: At a joint/end of a 2D (plane) frame member, there is only one transverse (shear) direction perpendicular to the member axis, so only one possible transverse shear force.

q: 3. At either end of a plane frame, maximum number of possible bending moments, are
explain: At a hinge/free end of a plane frame member, no bending moment can be resisted, hence the number of possible bending moments at such an end is zero (though for a fixed connection it can be one — as per book's stated answer for this variant, zero).

q: 4. If a constant section beam is subjected to a uniform bending moment throughout, its length bends to
explain: Under a uniform (constant) bending moment, the curvature (1/R = M/EI) is constant along the length, so the beam deforms into a circular arc of constant radius.

q: 5. The amount of temperature stress is .......... in fixed beam if compared with propped cantilever.
explain: A fixed beam provides total constraint at both ends, whereas a propped cantilever may allow some relief of stress depending on the specific support conditions and degrees of freedom.

q: 6. The maximum bending moment for a simply supported beam with a uniformly distributed load w/unit length is
explain: For a simply supported beam under UDL w per unit length, the maximum bending moment (at midspan) is wl²/8, a standard result.

q: 7. A simply supported beam carries varying load from zero at one end and w at the other end, the length of the beam is a, the maximum bending moment will be
explain: For a linearly varying load, maximum bending moment occurs at x=a/√3 from the zero-load end and evaluates to Wa²/(9√3), the standard closed-form result.

q: 8. Find the bending moment at fixed end of cantilever as shown in fig.
explain: The moment is calculated by the sum of forces times their distances (5T × 2m + 10 Tm = 20 Tm).

q: 9. Of the several prismatic beams of equal lengths, the strongest in flexure is one having the maximum
explain: Bending strength (moment carrying capacity for a given allowable stress) is M = σ×Z, so the beam with maximum section modulus Z is the strongest in flexure.

q: 10. Find the bending moment at 1/4th of the span having simply supported beam with following data: point load = 200 kg at centre, span = 20m
explain: Reaction at support is 100 kg. At x = 5m (1/4th span), BM = 100 kg × 5m = 500 kg-m.

q: 11. A simply supported beam of span L carries a uniformly distributed load, w. The maximum shear force, V is
explain: For a simply supported beam with UDL, the total load is wL. This is distributed equally to both supports, making the maximum shear force at the supports V = wL/2.

q: 12. A simply supported beam of span L carries a uniformly distributed load, w. The maximum bending moment, M is
explain: The maximum bending moment for a simply supported beam with a UDL occurs at the center and is calculated as M = wL²/8.

q: 13. A beam is hinged at both ends and loaded with a triangular load having maximum intensity (W) at centre. Find the maximum bending moment & shear force
explain: For a triangular load (reaching peak W at center) on a simply supported span L, the total load is WL/2, the reactions are WL/4, and the peak moment at the center is WL²/12.

q: 14. The shape of bending moment diagram over the length of a beam, carrying a uniformly increasing load is
explain: A uniformly increasing load (triangular) results in a parabolic shear force (2nd degree) and a cubical bending moment diagram (3rd degree).

q: 15. The maximum bending moment due to moving load on a simply supported beam occurs
explain: For a single moving point load on a simply supported beam, the maximum bending moment always occurs directly under the load position.

q: 16. The maximum deflection in the cantilever beam carrying a point load (W) at end is
explain: Standard structural formula for a cantilever with a point load at the free end: δ = WL³ / 3EI.

q: 17. The bending moment is maximum on a section where shear force
explain: Mathematically, dM/dx = V. When the shear force (V) is zero or changes sign, the derivative of the moment is zero, indicating a local maximum or minimum.

q: 18. For any types of loading, the no. of point of contraflexture in a simply supported beam is
explain: In a simply supported beam, the bending moment usually maintains the same sign (sagging) throughout the span, so there are zero points of contraflexure.

q: 19. When a rectangular beam is loaded longitudinally, shear develops
explain: Longitudinal loading (axial) typically creates uniform stress, but internal shear can be considered present across horizontal planes depending on the distribution of load.

q: 20. If the shear force along a section of a beam is zero, the bending moment at the section is
explain: As dM/dx = V, if V=0, the bending moment is at a stationary point, which is typically the maximum (or minimum) value in the region.

q: 21. For a beam of uniform strength, if width is constant
explain: Since bending stress σ ∝ M/(bd²) must remain constant with b fixed, d must vary as √M for uniform strength.

q: 22. Beams of composed of more than one material, rigidly connected together so as to be one piece are known as
explain: Beams made of two or more different materials rigidly bonded together to act as a single unit are termed composite beams.

q: 23. Find the DSI of propped cantilever beam
explain: A propped cantilever has 4 reaction components (3 at fixed end + 1 at prop). With 3 equilibrium equations, the Degree of Static Indeterminacy (DSI) is $$4 - 3 = 1$$.

q: 24. The simultaneous equations of slope deflection method can be solved by iteration in
explain: The Moment Distribution Method is essentially an iterative procedure for solving the same equations found in the slope-deflection method.

q: 25. Slope deflection method is
explain: The slope deflection method is a 'displacement method' or 'deflection method' where unknown joint displacements (slopes and deflections) are treated as the primary unknowns.

q: 26. A cantilever beam is the one which is supported with
options: one end hinge and other on rollers
one end fixed and the other on rollers
one end fixed and the other free
explain: By definition, a cantilever beam is fixed (built-in) at one end while the other end is completely free.

q: 27. Which of the following beams will have points of contraflexure?
options: A simply supported beam with udl over entire span
An overhanging beam with loading only over supported span and not on overhangs
Fixed beam subjected to concentrated load
Cantilever subjected to uniformly varying loads
explain: A fixed beam under a concentrated load develops both hogging moments near supports and sagging moment mid-span, so the bending moment changes sign, creating points of contraflexure.

q: 28. A beam is said to have been subjected to a pure bending moment, when
options: the load is applied as a udl throughout the span
S.F. in a length is zero
the load is applied at the mid-span section only
explain: Pure bending occurs over a length where shear force is zero (since dM/dx = SF), leaving only a constant bending moment.

q: 29. The line of thrust of the linear arch is
options: the imaginary line of thrust for a given set of loads
explain: For a given set of loads, the linear arch (or theoretical arch) follows the shape of the funicular polygon, which represents the imaginary line of thrust.

q: 30. If there is a cantilever beam joined with the edge of the span, then it is
explain: Joining a cantilever to an existing span introduces additional redundant constraints or internal forces that cannot be solved by simple static equilibrium equations alone, making the structure indeterminate.

q: 31. Influence line is
options: the line showing stress function due to unit moving load
the line showing stress function due to unit load
the line showing stress function due to udl
explain: By definition, an Influence Line Diagram (ILD) represents the variation of a specific response (stress function like shear, moment, or reaction) at a fixed section as a unit load moves across the structure.

q: 32. Which one is right w.r.t. ILD?
options: it is the BMD due to unit load
it is the BMD due to static unit load
it is the BMD due to moving unit load
it is the BMD due to impacting unit load
explain: The ILD specifically captures the effects of a moving unit load. Unlike a standard BMD which shows the effect of a fixed load along the whole beam, the ILD shows the effect at one spot for all possible load positions.

q: 33. The influence line diagram for reaction at a support of a simply supported beam is
options: a triangle with ordinate 1 at that support
a triangle with ordinate 1 at the other support
explain: For a support reaction $R_A$, the reaction is 1 when the unit load is exactly at A, and 0 when it is at the other support B. This creates a right-angled triangle with a peak (ordinate) of 1 at support A.

q: 34. A beam is completely analyzed when
options: shear and moment diagrams are found
the moment of inertia is uniform throughout the length
explain: A beam analysis is considered complete once the shear force and bending moment diagrams (which describe internal forces along the entire length) are obtained.

q: 35. A frame is completely analyzed when
options: the variation in shear is found throughout the frame
the variation in direct stress, shear and moment is found throughout the frame
the shear and moment reaction from member to member are known at every joint
explain: A rigid frame analysis is complete only when all three internal force quantities—axial (direct) force, shear force, and bending moment—are known throughout every member.

q: 36. For the beam shown in figure, the shear force at A is equal to (refer to image 1667):
explain: For a beam with a triangular load (zero at A, peak at B), the total load is $wl/2$ and the reaction at the lighter end A is $wl/6$.

q: 37. The load, required to produce a unit deflection in a spring is called :
explain: Stiffness ($k$) is defined as Force per unit displacement ($F/\delta$).

q: 38. When a load on the free end of a cantilever beam is increased, failure will occur
options: in the middle of the beam
at a distance 2l/3 from free end
explain: For a cantilever, bending moment is maximum at the fixed (built-in) support, so failure (due to maximum bending stress) will initiate there.

q: 39. A slab is a
explain: A slab has length and width much larger than its thickness, classifying it as a two-dimensional structure.

q: 40. The shear force diagram for a simply supported beam carrying a uniformly distributed load of w per unit length, consists of
explain: For a UDL on a simply supported beam, shear force varies linearly from +wl/2 to −wl/2, forming two right-angled triangles (positive on one half, negative on the other).

q: 41. In a simply supported beam carrying uniformly distributed load w per unit length, the point of contraflexure
options: lies in the centre of the beam
lies at the ends of the beam
depends upon the length of beam
explain: A simply supported beam under UDL has a bending moment that is always sagging (positive) throughout its span, never changing sign, so no point of contraflexure exists.

q: 42. The moment diagram for a cantilever whose free end is subjected to a bending moment, will be a
explain: A pure moment applied at the free end of a cantilever produces a constant bending moment throughout its length, giving a rectangular BMD.

q: 43. When a single load W moves over a simply supported beam, the maximum bending moment at a section will occur when the load is placed
explain: For a single moving load, the bending moment at a given section is maximum precisely when that load is positioned directly over the section itself.

q: 44. A straight beam subjected to pure bending will be bending in the shape of
explain: Under pure (constant) bending moment, the curvature 1/R = M/EI is constant along the length, causing the beam to deform into a circular arc.

q: 45. Which of the following sections is the most efficient in carrying bending moments?
explain: An I-section concentrates most material in the flanges, far from the neutral axis, maximizing the section modulus for a given area, making it the most efficient shape in bending.

q: 46. Shear force for a cantilever carrying a uniformly distributed load over its length, is
explain: For a cantilever under UDL, shear force varies linearly from zero at the free end to maximum at the fixed end, giving a triangular SFD.
